findings.explanation: Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux ships no linux:cgroup:memory or linux:psi:memory sourcetypes and no cgroup or PSI scripted input; a reader would look for inputs that do not exist. The same claim repeats in dataSources, app, and detailedImplementation ('Splunk_TA_nix versions differ across forwarder fleets', 'wiki mapping Splunk_TA_nix release notes to field renames').
findings.quote: Deploy Splunk_TA_nix scripted inputs for sourcetype=linux:cgroup:memory (memory.current, memory.max, memory.stat) and sourcetype=linux:psi:memory
findings.suggested_fix: State that the cgroup and PSI readers are custom scripted inputs (for example a script that walks /sys/fs/cgroup/system.slice/docker-<id>.scope and reads memory.current, memory.max, memory.stat and memory.pressure), optionally packaged alongside Splunk_TA_nix; remove the TA release-note field-rename narrative.

findings.explanation: On cgroup v2, an unlimited memory.max reads as the literal string "max", not a huge integer; the 9223372036854771712 sentinel is the cgroup v1 memory.limit_in_bytes behaviour. Readers building the collector or validating unlimited containers would look for the wrong value (also repeated in Step 2 'When memory.max returns the maximum pseudo-value').
findings.quote: confirms limit metadata when memory.max reads as the huge pseudo-infinity value
findings.suggested_fix: Say that cgroup v2 reports "max" for unlimited containers, which tonumber() turns into null, so mem_pct is null for those containers; mention the large-integer sentinel only for cgroup v1 memory.limit_in_bytes.

findings.explanation: latest=@h excludes up to the last 59 minutes of data and the window only advances hourly, so a five-minute schedule reprocesses the same hour twelve times and cannot deliver the 'five-to-thirty minute runway' promised in detailedImplementation and grandmaExplanation.
findings.quote: Save container_uc_3_1_4_memory_pressure every five minutes on earliest=-1h@h latest=@h
findings.suggested_fix: Recommend a rolling window such as earliest=-70m latest=@m (or -1h@m to @m), alert only on the most recent minute bucket per container, and throttle on host_id plus container_id.

findings.explanation: Container memory utilization is a host/cgroup performance metric; Application_State (service and process state inventory) does not fit the signal, and the cimSpl does not use it.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Performance only (Memory dataset), and remove Application_State from cimModels and dataModelAcceleration. Check whether Application_State is deprecated in the current CIM release before citing it anywhere.

findings.explanation: No Cloudflare source is referenced, the Datadog reference is the blog index page (https://www.datadoghq.com/blog/) rather than an article, and 'patterns documented by major cloud vendors' names nothing. This reads as filler.
findings.quote: External grounding includes Cloudflare and Datadog engineering write-ups on container memory pressure semantics, Linux kernel PSI documentation, and JVM heap-near-limit production patterns documented by major cloud vendors.
findings.suggested_fix: List only the specific sources actually referenced, and replace the Datadog blog index with the exact article URL or remove it.

findings.explanation: Authoring checklist residue that addresses the generator, not the implementer; it even claims an equipmentModels field the sidecar does not have. Similar filler: 'Training alignment', 'Documentation alignment', 'Governance alignment' paragraphs and 'fifty thousand containers'.
findings.quote: Closing checklist: monitoringType lists Performance and Capacity; splunkPillar Observability; equipment lists docker and linux; equipmentModels lists linux_cgroup_v2 and docker_engine; cimModels includes Performance; five step headers use plain em dash titles; Step 3 fenced SPL matches the spl JSON field exactly
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the closing checklist, the 'Fenced SPL ... byte-for-byte' note and the alignment paragraphs; keep collector, validation and troubleshooting content.

findings.explanation: Marked verified by a generic repository handle with no SME sign-off, while the SPL contains a tier that cannot fire and the collection path is misattributed.
findings.suggested_fix: Set status to draft/community until a reviewer validates the SPL against real cgroup v2 and PSI events.

findings.explanation: The semconv runtime section covers language runtimes (JVM, Go, Node.js), not container metrics; container memory metrics are documented under the system/container semantic conventions.
findings.quote:
OpenTelemetry — Runtime semantic conventions for container metrics",
      "url": "https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/runtime/"
findings.suggested_fix: Point to the OpenTelemetry container metrics semantic conventions page and retitle accordingly; update the Docker resource-constraints URL to its current docs.docker.com/engine/containers/resource_constraints/ location.

findings.explanation: Server models are irrelevant to cgroup memory accounting and read as invented specificity; the sentence also says 'memory.pressure files exist under delegated systemd slices', which is the only relevant requirement.
findings.quote: Dell PowerEdge R750, HPE ProLiant DL360 Gen11, Lenovo ThinkSystem SR650 V3, and AWS Graviton m7g fleets
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with the real prerequisites: Linux kernel 4.20+ with PSI enabled, unified cgroup v2 hierarchy, and Docker using the systemd cgroup driver.

findings.explanation: 'cgroup' is technical jargon in a plain-language field.
findings.quote: how full the cgroup allowance is
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'how full each workload's memory allowance is'.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: streamstats current=t global=f last(mem_pct) AS prev_mp BY host_id, container_id returns the current row's own mem_pct (last value in a window that includes the current event), so mem_jump is always 0 and the sudden_spike / high_sudden_spike_above_30pct_jump tier can never fire. Use current=f window=1 to get the previous minute.

The search emits every qualifying minute bucket over the hour (not just the latest), and low_baseline_drift_or_under_utilized fires for every minute any container sits below 30 percent, flooding alert output; latest=@h with a five-minute schedule repeats identical results. The mem_pressure_pattern hover rule uses anon >= 60 while the severity rule uses >= 70, and anon_b coalesces inactive_anon (a subset of anon) as if it were total anon.

The 9223372036854770000 guard targets the cgroup v1 unlimited sentinel; on cgroup v2 memory.max is the string "max", so the guard is dead code there (harmless, but misleading next to the cgroup-v2-only comment).

nodename=Performance.Memory, Performance.mem_used_percent and Performance.host are not valid CIM Performance paths; the root dataset is All_Performance (Memory child is All_Performance.Memory, host field is All_Performance.dest). Confirm the memory percentage field name against the CIM Performance reference.

summary: A thoughtful predictive memory-pressure design (cgroup v2 ratio, slope, PSI, anon share), but it attributes custom collectors to Splunk_TA_nix, misstates how cgroup v2 reports an unlimited memory.max, its SPL cannot produce the sudden-spike tier, the CIM search uses non-existent dataset paths, and the hourly-aligned window undercuts the claimed minutes-ahead runway.
